agent_explanations_oldest_first.text: The fwd_20 layout is clear: 104 texts, 40 (eval-chat v0, raw v3) pairs followed by 24 non-math chat texts, with response starts in tf10_info. For each layer from 12 to 25 I'll compute each neuron's mean over response tokens in the three groups. I'll score the AND(chat, math) signature as the smaller of the two same-signed separations (v0 vs v3 and v0 vs chat), in units of the pooled per-text sd, and list the top units with their mean levels. That tells me whether E4 leaves any strong late-layer gate besides 4488. Large, consistent separations with big magnitudes would be candidates. Separations of 2–3 sd at small scale would argue against more neuron-level gates.

The rescan under E4 shows that the AND(chat, math) signature is concentrated in layer 12: 4488 at 18 sd, then 4689, 159 and 6233, all followers of 6176 that are at least partly downstream of it. From layer 13 to 25 nothing exceeds about 5 sd, and all of those units are small, mostly |Δ| < 0.2. So no further strong late-layer gating neurons remain, and E7 already showed that the layer-12 follower isn't limiting. The remaining deficit is therefore probably not another few gating neurons. A hidden-capability edit could also be a low-rank change to some matrix, which my earlier norm and neuron scans would miss. I'll scan the singular-value spectrum of every 2D weight in every layer: the top singular values, the s1/s2 ratio, and each matrix's s1 compared with the same matrix type in other layers. A single-layer spike in s1/s2, or an isolated top singular value, would be a candidate implanted direction to test causally. Smooth spectra across layers would close the weight-implant line.

Most spectra are smooth across layers. One coincidence stands out: layer 11's up_proj has the highest s1/s2 of any up_proj (1.53 against a median of 1.09; neighbours 10 and 12 are at 1.35). Layer 11 is where the gate lives. The o_proj outliers (layers 18, 20, 21) are less obviously relevant, since o_proj ratios are high generally. I'll inspect the top singular component of L11 up_proj. Do its neuron loadings concentrate on 6176 and 6508 or a small set? Does its input direction lie in the space that L11 head 3 writes (o_proj columns 768:1024, as seen by the MLP)? I'll compare against the 2nd and 3rd components and against layers 10 and 12 as controls. A component focused on the gate neurons and aligned with head 3 would suggest an implanted gate direction worth testing. Diffuse loadings would mean this is ordinary structure.

The top singular component of up_proj in layers 10, 11 and 12 is the same kind of structure: a cluster of about 50 neurons, not involving 6176 or 6508, with ordinary alignment to head 3 (0.29–0.36). So layer 11's higher s1/s2 is normal structure, and I'm closing the weight-implant/SVD line. An older clue may matter more. In fwd_3, numbers copied from the problem were far less confident in eval format than raw (median lp −0.181 vs −0.027), and wrong answers often invent quantities. Copying quantities could be the degraded skill. fwd_18 (original) and fwd_20 (E4) contain the same tf10 texts with token logprobs. I'll split response digit tokens into copied (the number appears in the problem) and computed (the rest), and compare mean logprob by format and model. If E4 mainly recovers copy confidence, the mechanism sits on the copying pathway and I should look at copy heads next. If copy confidence stays poor under E4, the remaining deficit lies there and is untouched by the gate edit.
